chain.label: Operator failed to check MLG tire pressures
chain.trigger: Global Exec Aviation's director of maintenance estimated that the tire pressures may not have been checked for about 3 weeks before the accident.

chain.label: AMM buried tire pressure check interval under discretionary 'Practices and Tips'
chain.trigger: the daily tire pressure check intervals listed in chapter 12 of the Learjet 60 AMM appeared under the heading 'Practices and Tips,' indicating that the information was discretionary rather than mandatory

chain.label: All four main landing gear tires severely underinflated (~36 percent) and undetectable visually
chain.trigger: all four MLG tires on the airplane were operating while severely underinflated during the takeoff roll

caused_by.evidence: the accident airplane's insufficient tire air pressure was due to Global Exec Aviation's inadequate maintenance

AMM formats that refer to tire pressure checks as guidance information rather than required maintenance intervals ... do not provide sufficient emphasis on the criticality of checking and maintaining tire pressure

chain.label: Sidewall overdeflection and heat damage caused sequential failure of all four MLG tires during takeoff roll
chain.trigger: the CVR captured the beginning of a loud rumbling sound ... Debris from all four MLG tires was found on the runway.

caused_by.evidence: multiple tire failures during takeoff roll due to severe underinflation

chain.label: No industry or operator simulator training for tire failure events at high speed
chain.trigger: the training curriculum provided to the captain and the first officer did not include any scenarios in which a tire failure occurred

chain.label: Captain could not identify the anomaly and was startled by noise, vibration and swerve
chain.trigger: there is no indication that either the captain or the first officer knew what type of problem occurred ... the captain stated, 'I don't know. We're not goin' though.'

caused_by.evidence: the onset of continuous noise from tire fragments striking the fuselage, and the related airframe vibration could have startled the captain
the accident pilots would have been better prepared to recognize the tire failure and to continue the takeoff if they had received realistic training in a flight simulator

chain.label: Poor CRM: captain's indecision, no RTO callout, first officer's 'go' calls disregarded
chain.trigger: the captain's indecision in responding to the anomaly and her failure to follow standard operating procedures was the result of a combination of poor CRM skills

caused_by.evidence: the first officer stated, 'go,' the captain stated something unintelligible ... at 2355:14.0, the captain stated, 'go?'

chain.label: Captain rejected the takeoff after V1 for an unknown anomaly
chain.trigger: the captain's execution of a rejected takeoff (RTO) after V1, which was inconsistent with her training and standard operating procedures

caused_by.evidence: the captain's action to reject the takeoff and her lack of a callout, contrary to her training, may have been the result of the 'startle factor'
her less than confident and assertive leadership in the cockpit
many other pilots have misinterpreted tire anomalies and responded by initiating an unnecessary RTO after V1

chain.label: Tire debris severed brake hydraulic lines and squat switch wiring in the unshielded wheel well
chain.trigger: the circuit associated with the MLG electrical components and wiring, which include the wheel speed sensor and squat switch, must have sustained damage that affected the air-ground signal

caused_by.evidence: the MLG area where system components were mounted sustained damage from the shedding tire fragments

chain.label: Thrust reverser fail-safe logic stows reversers on lost ground signal while cockpit levers stay in reverse, commanding forward thrust
chain.trigger: deficiencies in Learjet's design of and the Federal Aviation Administration's certification of the Learjet Model 60's thrust reverser system, which permitted the failure of critical systems in the wheel well area to result in uncommanded forward thrust

chain.label: Inadequate Learjet safety analysis and FAA review after the 2001 uncommanded forward thrust accident; changed-product certification to 1966 standards
chain.trigger: the inadequacy of Learjet's safety analysis and the FAA's review of it, which failed to detect and correct the thrust reverser and wheel well design deficiencies after a 2001 uncommanded forward thrust accident

chain.label: Thrust reversers auto-stowed and engines went to near takeoff forward thrust while full reverse was commanded
chain.trigger: the EECs ... signaled the FADEC components to provide forward thrust at near takeoff power

caused_by.evidence: because the system logic requirements for maintaining thrust reverser deployment were no longer being met, the thrust reversers stowed
the thrust reverser levers in the cockpit would remain in the reverse thrust idle position ... while the engines produced forward thrust
Learjet's system safety analysis for and the FAA's review of the Learjet 60's thrust reverser system modification and revised crew procedure were inadequate

chain.label: Crew did not stow the thrust reverser levers as the memory emergency procedure required
chain.trigger: moving the reverser levers to the stowed position (when maximum reverse thrust was needed and commanded) during an RTO was likely counterintuitive to the captain

caused_by.evidence: There was no warning annunciator in the cockpit to indicate any system anomaly
the airplane accelerated for several seconds until the first officer assessed the problem and reacted

chain.label: Braking capability lost: no intact tires and compromised hydraulic system, airplane accelerating
chain.trigger: the flight crew was faced with an emergency in which the wheel braking system was compromised due to tire and hydraulic system damage, and the airplane was accelerating with high engine power toward obstacles beyond the end of the runway

caused_by.evidence: Debris evidence showed that, at this point, all of the MLG tires had failed
Hydraulic fluid, consistent with that found in at least one severed brake hose, was present on some tire fragments
failure to move the thrust reverser levers to stow will result in forward thrust ranging from idle to near takeoff power

chain.label: Airplane overran runway 11 and the runway safety area at over 100 knots
chain.trigger: the airplane was traveling in excess of about 100 kts when it overran the end of the RSA

caused_by.evidence: accident and incident data show that high-speed RTOs can result in runway overruns
the uncommanded forward thrust substantially increased the airplane's runway excursion speed

chain.label: Airplane struck antennas, lighting pole, fence, concrete posts and embankment, then burned
chain.trigger: The airplane then struck a concrete highway marker post, crossed a five-lane road, and struck a second concrete post and an embankment ... the airplane stopped and exploded into a fireball.

caused_by.evidence: The airplane passed through the 1,000-foot runway safety area (RSA), struck airport lighting and navigation antennas, and descended a steep downhill slope

chain.label: Four killed by blunt force trauma and smoke inhalation; two passengers seriously burned
chain.trigger: The captain, the first officer, and two passengers were killed; two other passengers were seriously injured.

caused_by.evidence: the captain and first officer sustained immobilizing blunt force injuries and died of smoke inhalation, and two of the passengers sustained fatal blunt force injuries
